title: Enforce retention boundaries for audit log exports + add export manifest warnings
author: Kevin Osei
body:
Context: Customers are asking for a clear, provable story that “exports respect retention.” Prior to this PR, the audit-log-exporter would export the requested time range as-is if the backing store still contained older partitions (e.g., delayed compaction, restore, or misconfigured TTL). That creates an inconsistency between (a) our stated retention window and (b) what a customer could export if they requested older ranges. This PR makes the exporter retention-aware by applying a server-side cutoff (effective retention boundary) and surfacing clear metadata/warnings in the export output so customers and auditors can understand what happened.

What’s in this PR: 1) Retention cutoff enforcement: For every export, compute an effective retention cutoff timestamp and clamp the export query to max(requested_start, cutoff). Records older than cutoff are never returned/exported even if present in storage. 2) Export manifest metadata: Every export zip now includes a manifest.json with retention-related fields and warnings when the requested range was partially outside retention (or when legal hold prevents deletion but export is still clamped). 3) API response warnings: The export-create response includes a non-fatal warnings array (also persisted into the export record) so UI/clients can show “partial export due to retention.” 4) Docs updates: Documented retention-aware export semantics, manifest format, and FAQ guidance for security reviews.

Retention boundary source: This service does not own the policy engine. The exporter calls Control Plane to fetch the effective retention policy for Audit Logs for the tenant + environment and uses that as the cutoff (now - retention_days). If Control Plane is unavailable, behavior is fail-closed for new exports (HTTP 503) rather than risk exporting beyond retention. This is aligned with Naomi/Marcus guidance from the security review thread.

Notes/edge cases: - Requested end < cutoff: returns 422 with a clear error (“requested range entirely outside retention”). - Requested start < cutoff <= requested end: export succeeds but is clamped; manifest contains warnings and the clamped range. - Legal holds: Export still respects retention boundaries for standard exports; legal hold impacts deletion, not export scope. We include a manifest note if the tenant has an active hold flag (for audit transparency) but do not expand exports beyond retention.

Testing: Added unit tests for cutoff computation and clamping, plus an integration-style test that validates manifest.json contents for clamped exports.

Release note: Audit log exports now enforce tenant retention windows and include retention metadata/warnings in an export manifest for auditability.

Screenshots: N/A (service + docs).

Rollout/compat: Backwards compatible. Existing clients can ignore the new warnings field and the extra file in the zip. Manifest file name is stable: manifest.json at zip root.

review_conversation: Marcus Lin (Security Eng) - 2025-02-12: I like the fail-closed behavior if we can’t fetch effective retention, but can we confirm we won’t break Private deployments where control plane connectivity is different? Also: wording on legal hold—make sure we don’t imply that legal hold expands export scope.

Kevin Osei (author) - 2025-02-12: Good call. For Private: the exporter talks to the local control plane endpoint (same as today for auth token introspection). I added a doc note and a test config stub. Re: legal hold wording—updated docs to explicitly state hold affects deletion/enforcement, not export scope, and added a manifest field “legal_hold_active” only as an informational flag.
Olga Petrov (GRC) - 2025-02-12: Can the manifest include the policy identifier and a clear statement that retention was applied? Auditors will want a stable artifact to point at.

Kevin Osei (author) - 2025-02-12: Yep. Added retention.policy_id and retention.applied=true plus retention.cutoff. Also included requested_range vs effective_range so it’s self-evident when clamping happened.

Dev Patel (Support) - 2025-02-13: From a customer experience perspective, what will clients see if they request a range entirely outside retention? Is 422 going to cause confusion? We should document the error and suggested resolution for SEs/support.

Kevin Osei (author) - 2025-02-13: Agreed. Added to docs/exports.md under “Common errors” with the exact message and recommended next step (“adjust start/end or update retention policy if eligible”). We can also add an FAQ entry later for Console UI behavior.

Fatima Noor (Regulated deployments) - 2025-02-13: Please confirm we’re not leaking retention values in cross-tenant contexts. Also: do we log cutoff timestamps anywhere that would become PII-ish? (It’s not, but just making sure we’re not logging request payloads.)

Kevin Osei (author) - 2025-02-13: Retention fetch is tenant-scoped (auth token includes tenantId; control plane enforces). Logs: we only log export_id + tenant_id + effective_start/effective_end (timestamps) at INFO and no query filters beyond that. No payload contents. I also downgraded a debug log that previously printed the entire request.
Marcus Lin (Security Eng) - 2025-02-14: One more thing: ensure the zip always contains manifest.json even when there are zero rows (export empty but valid). That’s important for evidence.
Kevin Osei (author) - 2025-02-14: Done. Manifest is written before row streaming; empty exports still have manifest + headers. Added a test case for zero-row export.
Olga Petrov (GRC) - 2025-02-14: Approved (thanks for the policy_id + applied flag).
release_notes: Audit log exports now enforce tenant retention windows server-side. Export zips include a manifest.json describing requested vs effective export ranges, the applied retention cutoff, and any warnings when a request is clamped.
